why: Design 7's dither made symmetric and given gain, aimed at the mid field. P is the phase switch (self 7, bias +3: on while Q < ~0.72, off once Q > ~0.90) and Pb its clean complement (sigmoid(4 - 8 P)). They push the wall +3 cos theta and -3 cos theta (P's and Pb's spokes), so the two phases sag alike as P's output does, mirror images. A and B read the uniform sum with negative spokes (-4), so their bias fits (-1.6), each lifted into range only in its own phase (A by +8 P, B by +8 Pb); a brighter phase makes its reader lower. Q (tau 12, bias 1.04) is driven by P (+1.06), A (+4) and B (-4). Phase lengths depend on how near Q's targets sit to P's thresholds (~0.5 in steady light), so a brighter forward phase (A lower) lasts longer and a darker backward phase (B higher) ends sooner: drift up the gradient. Q's drive from P equals the sum of P's thresholds in Q's units (-0.1 + 1.16), which keeps the phases equal in steady light; the readers' common level sets the phase length. S1-S3 adapt as before. Expected: steering in the mid field (~0.5 R/tick by calculation at 2,500 R), little in the far field.
